hints: Focus on where the excess fertiliser goes when very soluble nitrogen compounds are washed off flooded paddy fields.
Remember that dissolved nitrates like $\text{NO}_3^-$ are a food source for algae, so runoff will boost algal growth in the fish pens.
Connect what happens when that extra algae dies and is broken down by bacteria to dissolved oxygen and then to fish survival.
walkthrough:
**Follow the Runoff**

Nitrogen-based fertilisers are very soluble in water. Excess applied to flooded paddies dissolves easily and is carried in runoff water straight into the fish pens.

Key idea:
$$\text{excess fertiliser (s)} \rightarrow \text{dissolved } \text{NO}_3^- \text{(aq) in runoff}$$

**Feed the Algae**

Nitrate ions are essential nutrients for plants and algae. A sudden supply causes eutrophication, a rapid bloom of algae in the fish pens. So statement 3 is correct.

**Use Up the Oxygen**

The algal bloom blocks light and soon dies. Aerobic bacteria decompose the dead organic matter and use up dissolved oxygen for respiration. So dissolved oxygen levels fall and statement 2 is correct.

Key idea:
$$\text{dead algae + O}_2 \text{(dissolved) } \xrightarrow{\text{bacteria}} \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Harm the Fish**

Fish need dissolved oxygen to respire. Low oxygen, plus toxins from decay and algal blooms, stresses and kills fish. So fish production decreases and statement 1 is correct.

Conclusion: all three statements 1, 2 and 3 follow from excess fertiliser.

options.A: Correct, because all three happen in sequence. Runoff nitrates cause increased algae (3), bacterial decay of algae depletes dissolved oxygen (2), and low oxygen reduces fish production (1). This is classic eutrophication.
options.B: Incorrect because it leaves out one true effect. Many students accept fish loss and low oxygen but forget that the trigger is the initial algal bloom fed by nitrates.
options.C: Incorrect because it leaves out decreased fish production. Students sometimes stop at algae and oxygen and miss the final economic and biological consequence for the fish pens.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only one effect. It correctly links pollution to fish but ignores the key intermediate steps of algal growth and oxygen depletion that explain why.
